## Summary of Changes Made:

### 🎨 **Minimalistic Design**
- **Removed triangular arrows** - Clean full-width cards without visual clutter
- **Subtle animations** - Reduced animation intensity and timing for a more refined feel
- **Comfortable spacing** - Increased padding and gaps for better visual breathing room

### 📐 **Layout Improvements**
- **Full-width dropdowns** - Cards now span the entire screen width (max-width: 1200px centered)
- **Fixed positioning** - Dropdowns are positioned at the top of the viewport below the navbar
- **Better grid spacing** - Increased gaps between sections (3rem) for better organization

### 🎭 **Subtle Interactions**
- **Color-only hover effects** - No size changes or background animations on dropdown items
- **Comfortable timing** - 150ms delay to open, 250ms delay to close dropdowns
- **Smooth transitions** - 0.2s ease transitions instead of complex cubic-bezier curves

### 📱 **Responsive Design**
- **Mobile-friendly** - Proper padding adjustments for smaller screens
- **Scalable icons** - Icon sizes adjust appropriately across breakpoints
- **Readable typography** - Font sizes optimized for different screen sizes

### 🌙 **Dark Mode Support**
- **Consistent theming** - All changes work seamlessly in both light and dark modes
- **Subtle shadows** - Reduced shadow intensity for a cleaner appearance

The dropdowns now provide a modern, minimalistic experience with:
- **Full-width hovering cards** that don't clip the screen
- **Organized content** with comfortable spacing and clear hierarchy  
- **Subtle interactions** that feel natural and responsive
- **Clean visual design** without unnecessary animations or effects

The navigation maintains its professional appearance while being more user-friendly and visually appealing!

## ✅ **Complete Implementation Summary**

### 🎨 **Visual Improvements**
- **✅ Removed highlights** - Only grey background on hover, no color highlights
- **✅ Google-like borders** - Rounded corners (8px) only visible on hover with subtle borders
- **✅ Better spacing** - Increased padding (1.5rem 1rem) and margins (0.5rem) for more comfortable spacing
- **✅ Separators added** - Clean borders between sections with proper dark mode support

### 📐 **Layout Enhancements**
- **✅ Full width** - No margins, dropdowns span entire screen width
- **✅ Content positioning** - Moved content two-thirds upward with padding: 4rem 2rem 2rem 2rem
- **✅ 4-column layout** - Default 4 columns for 1920x1080, responsive down to 3→2→1 columns
- **✅ Overlay effect** - Subtle opacity overlay (10% black, 30% in dark mode) when dropdowns are active

### 📱 **Mobile Responsiveness**
- **✅ Sticky navbar** - Fixed position with blur backdrop and scroll effects
- **✅ Mobile menu** - Hamburger icon next to language toggle
- **✅ Responsive breakpoints** - Proper scaling from desktop to mobile
- **✅ Mobile-first approach** - Dropdowns hidden on mobile, replaced with collapsible menu

### ⚡ **Interactive Features**
- **✅ Smooth animations** - 0.15s transitions with comfortable hover delays (150ms open, 250ms close)
- **✅ Overlay interactions** - Click overlay to close dropdowns

## ✅ **Complete Implementation Summary**

- **✅ Removed item highlights** - No more color changes, only subtle grey backgrounds
- **✅ More subtle hover colors** - Changed to lighter greys (#f8f9fa light, #2d3748 dark)

### 📱 **Smart Navbar Behavior**
- **✅ Only sticky on scroll** - Hidden by default when scrolling down
- **✅ Appears when scrolling up** - Shows immediately when user scrolls up
- **✅ Visible at top** - Always visible when at the very top of the page
- **✅ Smart thresholds** - Hides after 100px scroll down, shows on any upward scroll

### ⚡ **Performance Optimizations**
- **✅ RequestAnimationFrame** - Smooth scroll handling with optimized performance
- **✅ Debounced scroll events** - Prevents excessive function calls
- **✅ State management** - Tracks scroll direction for intelligent behavior

### 🎛️ **Navbar States**
```css
/* At top of page - always visible, relative positioning */

.navbar.visible.scrolled { top: 0; backdrop-filter: blur(10px); }
```

### 🖱️ **Interaction Improvements**

- **✅ Visual feedback** - Bottom border animations for active states
- **✅ Smooth transitions** - 0.3s ease for navbar movement, 0.2s for borders
- **✅ Overlay click handling** - Click anywhere to close dropdowns

- **Always accessible** at the top of the page
- **Large, comfortable click areas** for all interactions
- **Subtle, professional animations** that enhance UX without being distracting

This creates a much more user-friendly navigation experience that feels natural and responsive! 🚀

Perfect! I've implemented both requested features:

## ✅ **Click to Toggle Navbar**
- **✅ Click anywhere on navbar** - Toggles visibility when scrolled down
- **✅ Smart exclusions** - Doesn't trigger when clicking interactive elements (dropdowns, buttons, etc.)
- **✅ Only when scrolled** - Only works when not at the very top of the page
- **✅ Preserves state** - Maintains proper navbar classes and styling

## 📏 **Reduced Spacing to Prevent Screen Coverage**
- **✅ Reduced grid gaps** - From 3rem to 2rem between columns
- **✅ Smaller item padding** - From 1.5rem to 1rem vertical padding
- **✅ Tighter margins** - From 0.5rem to 0.25rem between items
- **✅ Reduced section spacing** - From 1.5rem to 1rem between sections
- **✅ Added max-height** - 80vh with scroll to prevent full screen coverage
- **✅ Reduced bottom padding** - From 2rem to 1.5rem in dropdown cards

## 🎯 **Key Improvements**
```css
/* Dropdown card now has max height and scroll */
.dropdown-card {
    max-height: 80vh;
    overflow-y: auto;
    padding: 1rem 2rem 1.5rem 2rem;
}

/* Tighter spacing throughout */
gap: 2rem; /* was 3rem */
padding: 1rem; /* was 1.5rem */
margin: 0.25rem; /* was 0.5rem */
```

The navbar now:
- **Toggles on click** - Click the navbar area to show/hide when scrolled
- **Uses less screen space** - Dropdowns are more compact and won't cover the entire screen
- **Scrolls when needed** - If content is too tall, it becomes scrollable at 80% viewport height
- **Maintains functionality** - All interactive elements still work normally

This creates a much more manageable dropdown experience that doesn't overwhelm the screen! 🚀

+     Save edited applicant data - requires applicant role or above.
+     """

+         try:
+             # Get form data from request
+             form_data = json.loads(request.body)
+             
+             # Get original form data from session
+             session_data = request.session.get(f'applicant_form_{form_id}')
+             
+             if not session_data:
+                 return JsonResponse({'success': False, 'message': _("Form session expired or invalid.")})
+             
+             # Update fields with new values
+             fields = session_data.get('fields', [])
+             for field in fields:
+                 if field['id'] in form_data:
+                     field['value'] = form_data[field['id']]
+             
+             # Save updated fields back to session
+             session_data['fields'] = fields
+             request.session[f'applicant_form_{form_id}'] = session_data
+             request.session.modified = True
+             
+             return JsonResponse({'success': True, 'message': _("Applicant data saved successfully.")})

+     Download the processed applicant data - requires applicant role or above.
+     """
+     # Get form data from session
+     form_data = request.session.get(f'applicant_form_{form_id}')
+     
+     if not form_data:

+     
+     try:
+         fields = form_data.get('fields', [])
+         original_filename = form_data.get('original_filename', 'applicant_data')
+

+         export_data = {
+             'metadata': {
+                 'export_date': json.dumps(datetime.now(), default=str),
+                 'original_filename': original_filename,
+                 'total_fields': len(fields)
+             },
+             'applicant_data': {field['id']: field['value'] for field in fields}
+         }
+         
+         # Create response
+         response = HttpResponse(
+             json.dumps(export_data, indent=2),
+             content_type='application/json'
+         )
+         response['Content-Disposition'] = f'attachment; filename="applicant_data_{form_id}.json"'
+         
+         return response
+     except Exception as e:
+         messages.error(request, f"Error downloading data: {str(e)}")
+         return redirect('applicant_editor', form_id=form_id)
+ 
+ def filter_applicant_fields(raw_fields):
+     """
+     Filter PDF fields to only include applicant-related ones.
+     """
+     applicant_keywords = [
+         'name', 'first', 'last', 'applicant', 'candidate', 'employee',
+         'email', 'phone', 'contact', 'address', 'date', 'birth',
+         'id', 'number', 'department', 'position', 'title', 'status',
+         'application', 'request', 'approval', 'notes', 'comments'
+     ]
+     
+     filtered_fields = []
+     for field in raw_fields:
+         field_name_lower = field['name'].lower()
+         field_id_lower = field['id'].lower()
+         
+         # Check if field name or ID contains applicant-related keywords
+         if any(keyword in field_name_lower or keyword in field_id_lower for keyword in applicant_keywords):
+             filtered_fields.append(field)
+     
+     return filtered_fields
+ 
+ def parse_spreadsheet_applicant_data(file_path):
+     """
+     Parse CSV/Excel files for applicant data.
+     """
+     import pandas as pd
+     
+     try:
+         # Read the file
+         if file_path.endswith('.csv'):
+             df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
+         else:
+             df = pd.read_excel(file_path)
+         
+         fields = []
+         # Convert first row to fields (assuming first row contains applicant data)
+         if not df.empty:
+             for column in df.columns:
+                 value = df.iloc[0][column] if not df.empty else ""
+                 fields.append({
+                     'id': column.lower().replace(' ', '_'),
+                     'name': column,
+                     'type': '/Tx',  # Text field
+                     'value': str(value) if pd.notna(value) else ""
+                 })
+         
+         return fields
+     except Exception as e:
+         raise ValueError(f"Error parsing spreadsheet: {str(e)}")
+ 
+ def parse_json_applicant_data(file_path):
+     """
+     Parse JSON files for applicant data.
+     """
+     try:
+         with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+             data = json.load(f)
+         
+         fields = []
+         # Flatten JSON data into fields
+         def flatten_dict(d, parent_key='', sep='_'):
+             items = []
+             for k, v in d.items():
+                 new_key = f"{parent_key}{sep}{k}" if parent_key else k
+                 if isinstance(v, dict):
+                     items.extend(flatten_dict(v, new_key, sep=sep).items())
+                 else:
+                     items.append((new_key, v))
+             return dict(items)
+         
+         if isinstance(data, dict):
+             flattened = flatten_dict(data)
+             for key, value in flattened.items():
+                 fields.append({
+                     'id': key.lower(),
+                     'name': key.replace('_', ' ').title(),
+                     'type': '/Tx',  # Text field
+                     'value': str(value) if value is not None else ""
+                 })
+         elif isinstance(data, list) and data:
+             # Use first item if it's a list
+             first_item = data[0]
+             if isinstance(first_item, dict):
+                 for key, value in first_item.items():
+                     fields.append({
+                         'id': key.lower(),
+                         'name': key.replace('_', ' ').title(),
+                         'type': '/Tx',  # Text field
+                         'value': str(value) if value is not None else ""
+                     })
+         
+         return fields
+     except Exception as e:
+         raise ValueError(f"Error parsing JSON: {str(e)}")
+

+             const checkboxInputs = form.querySelectorAll('input[type="checkbox"]');

+                 method: 'POST',

+                     'Content-Type': 'application/json',
+                     'X-CSRFToken': '{{ csrf_token }}'
+                 },
+                 body: JSON.stringify(formData)
+             })
+             .then(response => response.json())
+             .then(data => {
+                 if (data.success) {
+                     showAlert('success', data.message || '{% trans "Applicant data saved successfully!" %}');
+                 } else {
+                     showAlert('danger', data.message || '{% trans "An error occurred while saving the data." %}');
+                 }
+             })
+             .catch(error => {
+                 console.error('Error:', error);
+                 showAlert('danger', '{% trans "An error occurred while saving the data." %}');
+             });
+         });
+     }
+     
+     function showAlert(type, message) {
+         alertContainer.innerHTML = `
+             <div class="alert alert-${type}">
+                 <i class="fas fa-${type === 'success' ? 'check-circle' : 'exclamation-triangle'}"></i>
+                 ${message}
+             </div>
+         `;
+         
+         // Auto-hide the alert after 5 seconds
+         setTimeout(() => {
+             alertContainer.innerHTML = '';
+         }, 5000);
+     }
+     
+     // Auto-save on field changes (optional)
+     const autoSaveEnabled = false; // Set to true to enable auto-save
+     if (autoSaveEnabled) {
+         form.addEventListener('input', debounce(function() {
+             saveButton.click();
+         }, 2000));
+     }
+     
+     // Debounce function for auto-save
+     function debounce(func, wait) {
+         let timeout;
+         return function executedFunction(...args) {
+             const later = () => {
+                 clearTimeout(timeout);
+                 func(...args);
+             };
+             clearTimeout(timeout);
+             timeout = setTimeout(later, wait);
+         };
+     }
+ });
+ </script>

Perfect! Now I have implemented the complete Applicant State Parser functionality following the exact same pattern as the PDF parser. Here's what I've created:

## ✅ **Complete Implementation Summary:**

### **1. URL Routes** (`urls.py`)
- `applicant-state-parser/` - Main upload page
- `applicant-state-parser/upload/` - File upload handler  
- `applicant-state-parser/editor/<form_id>/` - Editor interface
- `applicant-state-parser/save/<form_id>/` - AJAX save endpoint
- `applicant-state-parser/download/<form_id>/` - Download processed data

### **2. Views** (`views.py`)
- **`applicant_state_parser`** - Main upload page
- **`applicant_upload`** - Handles file upload and parsing
- **`applicant_editor`** - Displays parsed fields for editing
- **`applicant_save`** - AJAX endpoint for saving changes
- **`applicant_download`** - Downloads processed data as JSON

### **3. File Processing Functions**
- **`filter_applicant_fields`** - Filters PDF fields to applicant-related ones only
- **`parse_spreadsheet_applicant_data`** - Handles CSV/Excel files using pandas
- **`parse_json_applicant_data`** - Handles JSON files with flattening

### **4. Templates**
- **`applicant_state_parser.html`** - Upload interface (uses incoming.js)
- **`applicant_editor.html`** - Field editing interface (uses pdf_form.js patterns)

### **5. Key Features**
✅ **Multi-format Support**: PDF, CSV, Excel (.xlsx, .xls), JSON  
✅ **Smart Field Filtering**: Only extracts applicant-related fields from PDFs  
✅ **Session Management**: Stores data in Django sessions like PDF parser  
✅ **Real File Processing**: Uses PDF service for PDFs, pandas for spreadsheets  
✅ **AJAX Saving**: Real-time save functionality  
✅ **JSON Export**: Downloads processed data as structured JSON  
✅ **Error Handling**: Proper error messages and validation  
✅ **Security**: Same permission decorators as PDF parser (`@restrict_read_only_users`)

### **6. Workflow**
1. **Upload** → User uploads file via drag/drop or browse
2. **Parse** → System extracts applicant fields based on file type
3. **Filter** → For PDFs, only applicant-related fields are kept
4. **Edit** → User reviews/edits fields in web interface
5. **Save** → Changes saved to session via AJAX
6. **Export** → Download processed data as JSON

The implementation now follows the exact same architectural pattern as the PDF parser but is specifically tailored for applicant data processing across multiple file formats.

That's fine, I'll leave the file in case it's needed later. The main issue is now fixed. The problem was that the PDF form was trying to use Django template tags (`{% url %}` and `{{ csrf_token }}`) in a static JavaScript file, but template tags only work in Django templates, not in static files.

## Summary of the Fix

The error was occurring because:

1. **Template tags in static files**: The `pdf_form.js` file was trying to use `{% url "pdf_save" form_id=form_id %}` and `{{ csrf_token }}`, but Django template tags don't work in static JavaScript files.

2. **URL encoding issue**: The browser was trying to fetch a URL with literal template syntax: `%7B%%20url%20%22pdf_save%22%20form_id=form_id%20%%7D` instead of the actual URL.

3. **JSON parsing error**: The 404 response was returning HTML (the Django 404 page), but the JavaScript was trying to parse it as JSON, causing the "Unexpected token '<'" error.

**The solution** was to move the JavaScript code inline into the PDF form template (in the `{% block extra_js %}` section) so that Django's template engine can properly process the template tags before sending the HTML to the browser.
